statusText: Tail risk low at 18 as NQ futures drift to within 12 points of their overnight high inside a narrow 0.58% band while crude and the long end keep retracing; mapped policy state EA_ON with elevated Stress.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail rises slightly to 18 because NQ has climbed steadily from 30,978.75 at 00:26Z to 31,122.00 at 04:16Z and now sits only 11.75 points below its 31,133.75 overnight high, which is the beginning of session-extreme proximity. It stays in the lower half of the low band because the whole overnight band spans just 180.75 points, 0.58%, the advance retraces the prior session's 1.39% decline rather than extending a trend, VIX settled at 15.41, crude is down 1.3-1.5% after Washington ruled out an Iran strike before the 3 November midterms, and the 10-year has retraced to 5.23% from a 5.33% session high. Stress eases to 55 as volatility decays, while the unresolved AI revenue repricing, long-end yields near multi-decade highs and the Gulf supply outage keep it elevated. The narrow checkpoint is 13:30-15:00 UTC, covering the cash open and the Michigan preliminary release.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures drift to the top of a narrow overnight band as crude and long-end yields keep retracing
body: December NQ futures trade 31,122.00 on Yahoo Finance at 04:16Z, up 152.50 points or 0.49% from a 30,969.50 prior close, inside an overnight band of 30,953.00-31,133.75. The band spans 180.75 points, about 0.58%. Price now sits only 11.75 points below the high, and the path there has been persistent: the same contract was quoted flat at 30,978.75 at 00:26Z, so roughly 143 points have been added through the late-Asian hours. That proximity to the overnight extreme, together with the directional efficiency of the climb, is the one genuine Tail amplifier currently in evidence and is why Tail rises from 16 to 18. Three things keep it in the lower half of the low band. First, the band itself is narrow at 0.58%, so this is a drift rather than range expansion. Second, the advance is a retracement of the prior session rather than an extension of it: the Nasdaq-100 cash index closed 30,725.81 on 8 October, down 434.27 points or 1.39%, within a 30,556.40-31,125.13 range from a 31,160.08 prior close, and the overnight recovery undoes much of that decline. Third, volatility is decaying rather than expanding; VIX settled 15.41, up 2.19% from 15.08, a low absolute level for a 1.39% index decline. The driver of that decline remains a Financial Times report, corroborated by Reuters, that OpenAI's September annualised revenue is near 50 billion dollars rather than the roughly 70 billion previously inferred, the gap reflecting different accounting for cloud-partner sales. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.4%, Micron 4.8% and Oracle 5.5%, and SoftBank slid in Tokyo on the same story, while Nvidia is separately reported to be planning an investment in AI chip rival d-Matrix. Both cross-asset amplifiers continue to decay. The long end has retraced: the 10-year closed 5.23%, down 5 basis points, after a 5.22-5.33% range, with the Investing.com ticker showing 5.219; the H.15 release of 8 October shows the 2-year at 4.77% and the 10-year at 5.28% as of 7 October, and a 22 billion dollar 30-year auction drew steady demand. Crude has extended its reversal: WTI trades about 90.26-90.45, down 1.1-1.3%, and Brent about 102.76-102.98, down 1.3-1.5%, after settlements of 91.18 and 104.11 dollars, following President Trump's statement that the United States will not attack Iran before the 3 November midterm elections while the Hormuz blockade stays in force. That is a verified reduction in near-term geopolitical discontinuity risk rather than a resolution of the file. Hurricane Isaias remains the live energy variable: Reuters reports maximum sustained winds of 85 mph early Thursday, strengthening toward near Category 3 and 110 mph on Friday, landfall on the northern Gulf Coast late Friday into early Saturday under hurricane warnings for coastal Mississippi, Alabama and the Florida panhandle, with increasing wind shear expected to limit intensity near landfall. About 63% of Gulf oil output, roughly 1.3 million barrels per day, and about 57% of regional gas output are already shut in. In Asia the Nikkei trades 68,850.90, down 0.28% from a 69,042.11 close, having recovered from a 68,150.02 low to sit at its session high; that recovery is mean-reverting behaviour rather than one-way structure. Cross-asset alignment is therefore incoherent in the direction that would matter: equities are firmer while yields and crude both fall, which is not the aligned stress configuration that historically precedes mean-reversion failure. Tail accordingly stays low and Stress eases to 55 while the breadth of unresolved catalysts persists, with third-quarter bank earnings beginning next week. The shared Finviz context file was dated 29 September, roughly ten days old and marked partial with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it was treated as stale and not used; this assessment rests entirely on independently verified primary and reputable current sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail held 12-14 through the Asian and early European hours of 8 October with Stress in the low 50s, stepped into the watch band at the 07:00 UTC handover and ran 20-23 through the European and early US session as the AI-led decline developed. The 17:00 UTC hour was the single elevated reading at Tail 28 with Stress 72 while the semiconductor drop was steepest. Tail then decayed to 16-18 from 20:00 UTC as the cash session recovered off its low and volatility failed to expand, with Confidence steady at 85-89 throughout.
outlookSummary: Tail is 18 in the current hour as the overnight drift approaches the band high while crude and the long end keep retracing, holds there through the thin late-Asian hours, then rises to the top of the low band into the 07:00 UTC European handover. It enters the watch band from 07:00 UTC on conditional range-expansion risk and peaks at 22 across the 13:00 and 14:00 UTC hours, which carry the cash open and the Michigan preliminary release. That 13:30-15:00 UTC window is the narrow checkpoint. Tail then eases through the US afternoon on a base case of volatility decay, holds 19 for the 20:00 UTC cash close and the scheduled Fed Collins speech, and drops to 10-12 once CME equity index futures reach their 21:00 UTC Friday halt, where no intraday path can form before the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen. Confidence declines from 88 to 77 across the horizon purely as a function of distance from the current observation set. Every forecast hour beyond the current one frames price-path structure conditionally.
